Selection context helpers

Source: R/selection-context.R
selection_context_validate.Rd

Validate and subset row-wise selection-kernel contexts and prepare small argument lists for native selected-normal backends.

selection_context_validate(context, n_samples = NULL, required = character())

selection_context_subset_rows(context, rows)

selection_context_subset_observations(context, idx)

selection_native_static_args(selection_spec)

selection_native_kernel_args(
  selection_spec,
  S,
  alpha = NULL,
  phack_kind = NULL,
  kernel_mode = NULL
)

selection_row_arg(x, n, name)

Arguments

context

selection context list.

n_samples

optional expected number of posterior/sample rows.

required

character vector of fields that must be present.

rows

row indices or logical row mask.

idx

observation indices.

selection_spec

selection backend specification or context list.

S

number of rows for row-wise native arguments.

alpha

optional p-hacking severity values.

phack_kind

optional p-hacking form indicators.

kernel_mode

optional selection-kernel mode indicators.

x

scalar or row-wise vector.

n

required row count.

name

argument name used in errors.

Value

selection_context_validate(), selection_context_subset_rows() and selection_context_subset_observations() return the context list with every field validated (integer codes as integer vectors, scalars expanded to one value per row) and its native cache reset by the subsetting functions; the native argument helpers return lists of prepared native arguments.

Details

Context validation checks row-wise posterior fields, observation fields, and compiled selection-bin metadata together. Custom row-wise fields may be listed in a character vector named row_fields; row subsetting rejects undeclared fields that otherwise look row-wise. The built-in vector_rule field accepts the integer codes 0 (product), 1 (best one-sided p-value), and 2 (best two-sided p-value), with one value or one value per posterior row. Native argument helpers accept either an augmented context or a bare selection_backend_spec() object, using compiled step, phacking, and data fallbacks where available. Spec-level kernel_mode is the union of branch kernels (a capability flag). Row routing uses branch_kernel_mode or an explicit per-row vector; the per-row kernel_mode (and phack_kind) of a context take precedence over the branch metadata, and an explicit argument over both. Branches with kernel mode 0 carry no selection kernel and never compete for a route, so a specification whose active branches all share one kernel routes on that kernel. When two or more different active kernels coexist, their bitwise union names a third kernel rather than a route, and passing it is an error unless bias_indicator can map each row to a branch. The built-in row fields, each of length one or one per posterior row, are omega (a numeric matrix of non-negative weights with one row per posterior row and one column per selection bin), alpha (the p-hacking severity, in [0, 1)), the integer codes phack_kind (0 to 2), kernel_mode (0 to 3), vector_rule (0 to 2), and bias_indicator (the index of the branch of each row, from 1 to the number of branches), and the logical use_normal. The observation fields share one length: obs_bin (the integer selection bin of each observation, from 1 to the number of bins), yi (finite effect sizes) and sei (positive standard errors). A fractional or missing integer code is an error, never rounded or truncated onto another code. Native caches are reused only when effective static geometry and complete row-routing inputs are unchanged. Explicit segments take precedence over p-value cuts; cuts are validated only when segments must be derived.
